candidate_relations.reason: Neonatal encephalopathy is a functional descriptor, not hydranencephaly.
Optic-nerve hypoplasia/pallor is an associated ocular finding, not the brain malformation.
Zellweger spectrum disorder is a different malformation syndrome not required by this post-twin-death disruption pattern.
Periventricular leukomalacia is a different white-matter injury pattern from near-hemispheric replacement by fluid.
Premature-birth complications do not name hydranencephaly; gestational age was late preterm.
IUGR with cerebral impairment is associated but is not hydranencephaly.
Cerebral visual impairment is a functional consequence of severe hemispheric loss.
Pseudotumor cerebri is an incompatible raised-pressure syndrome; there was no elevated intracranial pressure.
Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy is a different muscle-eye-brain syndrome without myopathy data here.
Muscle-eye-brain disease is not supported by the preserved brainstem/cerebellum disruption pattern after co-twin death.
Monochorionic diamniotic twinning complications supply the likely vascular cause of hydranencephaly but not the malformation name.
Pompe disease is a different metabolic myopathy unrelated to this MRI pattern.
Hydrocephalus with brainstem preservation is the classic related mimic with incompatible residual-cortex/hydrodynamic identity from hydranencephaly.
Fetal akinesia deformation sequence is a different phenotype not described.
Prenatal brain disruption sequence is the mechanistic parent class of hydranencephaly but missing that specific phenotype.
Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome is a different malformation syndrome.
Septo-optic dysplasia is a related midline/optic malformation, not massive hemispheric destruction with preserved deep structures.
Peroxisomal biogenesis disorder is not the post-ischemic disruption pattern after co-twin demise.
Fetal growth restriction is an associated obstetric finding, not hydranencephaly.
Cerebral dysgenesis is a parent brain-malformation label missing hydranencephaly.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; hydranencephaly is not named
